newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks remain up, but slipping on malaise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks remain up, but slipping on malaise.

text.p: Taiwan share prices were higher but slipping from earlier peaks at mid-session on Friday as the caution-laden market again showed an inability to sustain gains, brokers said.
With 80 minutes left, the weighted index was up 19.73 points or 0.25 percent at 8,017.38, off an intra-day high of 8,058.21.
Turnover was a modest T$41.57 billion.
Financials rose 0.83 percent on the government's final approval of the privatisation scheme for the "big three" state-run commercial banks.
"The privatisation news gave a mild boost to financials, but it is not enough to elevate the overall market," said George Hou, a fund manager for Jardine Fleming.
"There really isn't a bullish factor significant enough to excite investors right now," Hou added.
